subject.title: fix(wechat): preserve existing accounts across hot reload

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose accountIndexReloadPaths as a channel-plugin reload contract, and if so is focused Gateway regression evidence sufficient for WeChat or is live A+B provider proof required before merge?
rationale: The implementation intentionally expands the plugin-facing reload API and the contributor cannot supply provider credentials or a live WeChat session; neither API permanence nor a proof waiver can be inferred from tests alone.

options.title: Approve the contract and require live proof
options.body: Confirm the new plugin reload capability, then require redacted exact-head evidence that adding WeChat account B leaves account A online.

options.title: Approve a focused-proof waiver
options.body: Confirm that the documented Gateway regressions and normal CI are sufficient for this narrowly scoped lifecycle behavior without provider credentials.

options.title: Pause the API addition
options.body: Keep the PR open or close it later if maintainers do not want this plugin contract in the current SDK surface.

recommendation.title: Approve the contract and require live proof
recommendation.body: Confirm the new plugin reload capability, then require redacted exact-head evidence that adding WeChat account B leaves account A online.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged adjacent reload work is the strongest available history signal for the Gateway/plugin reload boundary.
